authority_chain_required: Property → Tenancy → Tenant(s) → Rent Schedule → Ledger Periods → Payments

findings.summary: Rent schedules were property-scoped with optional unvalidated tenancy_id; UI created schedules with property_id + free-text tenant_name only.
evidence: create_rent_schedule deactivated all active schedules per property, not per tenancy
ledger period dedupe used (client_id, property_id, period_key) ignoring schedule_id
Rent Operations page was authority source for schedule creation without tenancy picker

findings.summary: Header Record payment allowed amount/date-only POST without ledger_id or tenancy_id.
evidence: RecordPaymentModal submitted property_id only when no ledger selected
rent_payments documents lacked tenancy_id before remediation

findings.summary: No hooks from tenancy lifecycle (move-out, replacement) to rent schedule closure or new lineage.
Superseded schedules left ledger rows; new schedule skipped existing period_keys on property causing amount/frequency drift.
Payment allocation by property_id without tenancy filter could allocate across tenancies on same property.
False failed-success: API could error after schedule insert while periods existed; UI showed generic failure.
evidence: No idempotency_key on schedule or payment create

remediation_summary: Introduced property_tenancies authority, mandatory tenancy_id (or disclosed external payer), schedule-scoped ledger materialisation, payment ledger-first authority, idempotent create, preview disclosure, unallocated payment persistence.
